campaign: Is It Actually Useful? Gadget Usefulness Scorecard

prospects.name: Make: article proposals
prospects.fit: Make accepts project, skill-builder, review, technology, drone, education, and photography article proposals with evidence that the project is built and functional.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch an original, visual skill-builder showing how to turn the scorecard into a repeatable real-gadget evaluation, using one genuinely documented example rather than promoting the website.
prospects.blocker: Verify the public guide and PDF, confirm rights to the example imagery, and prepare the project image the form requires.

prospects.name: Core77 website submissions
prospects.fit: Core77 explicitly reviews submitted URLs, short descriptions, and community projects for editorial inclusion across its industrial-design publication.
prospects.firstAsk: Offer the evidence-led scorecard as a transparent product-evaluation framework and invite editorial critique of the problem-fit, proof, cost, friction, and support model.
prospects.blocker: Verify the guide and printable publicly, then prepare a design-focused description and complete visual package without claiming scientific validation.

prospects.name: PetaPixel story pitches
prospects.fit: PetaPixel's contact route accepts tips and story pitches and can consider owned blog material for an attributed guest post when republication permission is explicit.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch a first-person camera or FPV field-test story that uses the scorecard to separate documented settings and footage from unknowns, with rights-cleared source frames.
prospects.blocker: Verify the site resource, recheck the live form, and decide whether any republication permission is appropriate for the exact article and images.

prospects.name: Fstoppers article suggestions
prospects.fit: Fstoppers exposes separate current routes for article suggestions and prospective contributors and expects technique-led reader value rather than self-serving promotion.
prospects.firstAsk: Propose an educational article about evaluating camera gear after a real field session, using Colin's original FPV footage and a reusable retest checklist as the practical takeaway.
prospects.blocker: Verify the linked resource and assemble an original technique-led pitch whose value stands without a backlink or promotional exchange.

prospects.name: DIY Photography guest posts
prospects.fit: DIY Photography currently invites tips, fresh guest-post ideas, and rights-confirmed article republication for its photography, video, gear, and learning audience.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch a fresh evidence-led camera-field-test article with original images and show how the scorecard prevents a first flight from becoming an overstated final review.
prospects.blocker: Verify the destination, select original rights-cleared material, and decide whether to pitch new work or grant bounded republication rights.

prospects.name: Laptop Mag freelance pitches
prospects.fit: Laptop Mag's pitch guide, updated in 2025, requests independent consumer-technology expertise, fresh angles, clips, and specific news, review, how-to, opinion, or feature ideas.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch an independently reported consumer-tech piece about the evidence buyers should demand after a compelling gadget demo, supported by concrete product examples and source interviews.
prospects.blocker: Verify the public framework, develop a publication-specific reported angle, and disclose every product or company relationship before pitching.

prospects.name: No Film School pitches
prospects.fit: No Film School accepts specific educational pitches grounded in personal filmmaking experience, including cinematography, production technology, sound, editing, and creative process.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch a first-person production-gear field note that teaches filmmakers how to separate a promising first session from a controlled review and plan the next useful test.
prospects.blocker: Verify the linked framework and select one documented production session with original footage, exact limitations, and a useful teaching outcome.

prospects.name: South Florida Venture Tech Chronicle contributors
prospects.fit: The current South Florida publication selectively accepts guest contributors and story ideas about technology, innovation, regional economic trends, and local creators.
prospects.firstAsk: Pitch a South Florida creator case study about building an evidence-led gadget and video series, emphasizing lessons, transparent measurement, and regional relevance rather than promotion.
prospects.blocker: Verify the guide, choose a genuinely regional narrative with measurable lessons, and recheck the contact route on the day of outreach.

prospects.name: Hackaday tips
prospects.fit: Hackaday accepts links to fresh, documented hacks and explicitly includes projects created by the person submitting the tip while rejecting generic press releases.
prospects.firstAsk: Submit only after Colin has a distinctive, fully documented hardware or software build whose problem, design decisions, failures, and evidence are useful without the scorecard link.
prospects.blocker: The standalone scorecard is not a hack; an original finished build and a rights-reviewed public write-up must exist first.

prospects.name: Cool Tools reader reviews
prospects.fit: Cool Tools invites reviews from real users and asks for at least six months of use, changed behavior, comparative experience, and a reason readers should trust the recommendation.
prospects.firstAsk: Contribute only a tool Colin has genuinely used long enough to answer every experience question, using the scorecard privately to strengthen the evidence rather than pitching the worksheet itself.
prospects.blocker: Colin must select a qualifying long-used tool and confirm that the current review form and compensation terms are acceptable.

prospects.name: Tampa Hackerspace classes
prospects.fit: The volunteer-run Tampa makerspace hosts public technology workshops, open make nights, and an explicit path for people interested in leading a class.
prospects.firstAsk: Ask whether a hands-on session comparing one real gadget's claims, evidence, cost, friction, and support would help members; seek instructor feedback before publicity.
prospects.blocker: Colin must choose to participate in a genuine local workshop relationship and prepare a practical demonstration rather than a promotional talk.

prospects.name: Tampa Devs speaker submissions
prospects.fit: Tampa Devs accepts software-community talk proposals and provides event production, a recorded YouTube talk, photography, and a referenceable blog entry for accepted speakers.
prospects.firstAsk: Propose a developer-focused talk about building trustworthy creator publishing and measurement systems, with concrete Angular and Firebase lessons rather than a consumer-gadget pitch.
prospects.blocker: This is a speaking commitment in an adjacent technical lane; Colin must approve the time, topic, and public presentation before submission.

prospects.name: TechFlo talks and partnerships
prospects.fit: TechFlo describes a South Florida technology community that invites speakers and organizational partners for talks, learning, growth, and professional connection.
prospects.firstAsk: Explore a practical creator-tech talk only if Colin wants a continuing South Florida relationship; lead with a useful demonstration and audience discussion, not a link request.
prospects.blocker: The site currently redirects and the event route must be rechecked; Colin must also approve a genuine speaker or community commitment.

prospects.name: Maker Faire Orlando exhibits
prospects.fit: Maker Faire Orlando's 2026 application invites individuals and community groups to demonstrate real projects and share what they made and learned at its public event.
prospects.firstAsk: Apply only with an interactive real-gadget evidence demonstration or finished build that visitors can inspect, score, question, and compare in person.
prospects.blocker: An exhibit requires an approved physical concept, November availability, staffing, rights clearance, and event-specific preparation.

prospects.name: Popular Mechanics freelance pitches
prospects.fit: Popular Mechanics maintains a current pitch guide for deeply reported technology stories and separately invites experienced product-review writers to discuss freelance opportunities.
prospects.firstAsk: Approach only with a timely, independently reported technology story or a clearly evidenced review beat; use the framework as process, not as the subject's sole novelty.
prospects.blocker: The present scorecard is not enough for this editorial bar; Colin needs a strong timely story, reporting plan, clips, and an explicit freelance commitment.

prospects.name: Yanko Design project submissions
prospects.fit: Yanko Design reviews original design projects submitted with a substantial description and at least five high-resolution images, subject to rights and editorial selection.
prospects.firstAsk: Consider only after the framework becomes a visually distinctive designed object or documented product concept with the complete image package the publication requests.
prospects.blocker: The printable worksheet alone is not yet a strong industrial-design project and lacks the required five-image presentation package.

prospects.name: IEEE Spectrum freelancer guidelines
prospects.fit: IEEE Spectrum accepts reported engineering stories, consumer-electronics coverage, multimedia, and DIY pitches with a strong technology narrative and explicit significance.
prospects.firstAsk: Hold until Colin has a genuinely reported engineering story with multiple sources, technical depth, international relevance, and a clear reason it matters now.
prospects.blocker: The scorecard is not a Spectrum engineering story and no qualifying reported narrative or interview plan exists yet.

prospects.name: WIRED story pitches
prospects.fit: WIRED publicly describes a selective freelance process centered on narrative technology, science, innovation, reporting, access, and faint signals of consequential change.
prospects.firstAsk: Do not pitch a worksheet; revisit only if Colin develops a deeply reported gadget or creator-technology narrative with characters, scenes, access, and wider consequence.
prospects.blocker: No WIRED-scale narrative, pre-reporting, access, or timely wider impact is currently established.

prospects.name: Smashing Magazine article pitches
prospects.fit: Smashing Magazine accepts practical experience-led web design and development outlines while explicitly rejecting content marketing, obvious product promotion, and most product reviews.
prospects.firstAsk: Use only for a separate Angular or creator-publishing case study with transferable implementation lessons; do not pitch the gadget scorecard to an unrelated audience.
prospects.blocker: The active gadget asset does not fit Smashing's professional web audience, and a distinct original technical outline would be required.

prospects.name: The Gadgeteer suggestions
prospects.fit: The Gadgeteer accepts gadget news and article suggestions, but its current review route is intended for product suppliers and its last visible reviewer recruitment is closed.
prospects.firstAsk: Recheck for a current independent contributor opening before proposing a practical evidence-led article; never use the product-review intake for a website resource.
prospects.blocker: No current guest-contributor route was verified, and Colin is not submitting a product for review.

prospects.name: Gear Diary review policy
prospects.fit: Gear Diary publishes consumer-perspective gear reviews with strong editorial-independence rules, but its current policy explicitly rejects guest reviews from random freelancers and brands.
prospects.firstAsk: Do not contact for this campaign unless a future public contributor route appears or Colin legitimately owns a product and seeks an independent review under their supplier policy.
prospects.blocker: The publication explicitly does not accept the type of guest review or resource pitch this campaign could offer.

prospects.name: Instructables project publishing
prospects.fit: Instructables lets registered creators publish documented step-by-step projects with text, images, video, files, categories, keywords, and optional contest entry.
prospects.firstAsk: Use only for a complete build that deserves a native step-by-step tutorial, and record it as self-publication rather than an earned editorial backlink.
prospects.blocker: No qualifying native build tutorial is prepared, an account action would be required, and self-publishing is not independent recognition.

prospects.name: Hackster.io project publishing
prospects.fit: Hackster supports public hardware projects and approved community hubs, but a discoverable platform hub requires an account, approval, and published-project and follower thresholds.
prospects.firstAsk: Revisit only with a complete hardware build and native documentation; classify any project page as community self-publication until independent editorial selection occurs.
prospects.blocker: The scorecard is not a hardware project, no Hackster account action is authorized, and hub thresholds are not met.

prospects.name: Gadget Flow product submissions
prospects.fit: Gadget Flow reviews submissions for market-ready products with dedicated commerce pages, lifestyle images, and video, and offers optional paid promotion after editorial review.
prospects.firstAsk: Do not submit the scorecard; revisit only if Colin launches a real available product and separately evaluates the free editorial review and any commercial terms.
prospects.blocker: The campaign asset is a free editorial worksheet rather than an ecommerce or crowdfunding product, so the current submission path is a category mismatch.

prospects.name: ArabTechGate paid guest posts
prospects.fit: The page covers gadgets and buying guides but advertises fixed-price guest-post packages tied to two or three dofollow links.
prospects.firstAsk: Do not contact or buy placement; retain this row as a negative-control example of a route that conflicts with the campaign's earned-authority rules.
prospects.blocker: Paid dofollow placement is prohibited by the outreach guardrails and should not be counted as editorial authority.
